views.label: Upload
views.note: Upload stores content-addressed nodes. It does not change the MMR.

views.label: Commit
views.note: Each primary signs a CommitmentPayload naming the bucket_id, agreement_id and genesis hash. The signature is the immediate guarantee.

views.label: Checkpoint
views.note: The chain checks that the commitment repeats or extends the snapshot or, for an admin deletion, starts a new MMR; it records the signers.

segments.label: Commit: provider signs the new MMR state

messages.label: same upload and commit
messages.note: primaries do not sync with each other

messages.label: GET /checkpoint-signature?bucket_id&agreement_id&prev_start_seq&prev_leaf_count
messages.note: signs the same CommitmentPayload; adds consistency_proof for an append

messages.label: extend_checkpoint(bucket_id, additional_signatures)
messages.note: anyone may call; adds late signers only

cards.title: Upload and commit are separate
items: Upload stores nodes; the MMR does not change
Commit adds data_roots; the provider is liable
Uploads within quota do not conflict

cards.title: Signature before checkpoint
items: A commitment names one agreement_id and the genesis hash; it is void when that agreement ends

cards.title: Multiple primaries
items: The client uploads to each primary
After checkpoint: prune a non-canonical branch once the canonical end is past its end
Virtual primary: a coordinator member fans the write out and returns at least k member signatures; in checkpoint they are all-or-nothing (at least k or none)
activate_replacements: set only to activate a pending replacement of a virtual provider; extend_checkpoint never activates one

cards.title: What a checkpoint may change
items: Identical: the snapshot's commitment again; its signers replace primary_signers
Append: same start_seq, larger leaf_count, and a consistency_proof (MmrConsistencyProof) that the snapshot's MMR is a prefix of the new one
Deletion, admin only: start_seq = snapshot start_seq + leaf_count, no proof; a new MMR with the kept leaves appended again
Every checkpoint meets min_providers on its own and replaces primary_signers; canonical history is linear
No snapshot counts as an empty MMR at start_seq 0; an empty MMR has mmr_root H256::zero()
